question: Which candidate will lead Alaska's U.S. Senate race in first-choice votes as of November 13, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Late-Oct first-choice polls show Peltola +1-2 (NYT/Siena 48-46, ASR 48-46, RCP +1.2); primary she led 49.5-41.4. Polymarket prices Peltola to win the seat (post-RCV) at ~74c ($2.5M volume), Kalshi ~71% — near-miss contract (final winner, not first-choice leader on Nov 13) but first-choice lead should be at least as likely for Peltola since Heikes and Sullivan Jr. siphon first-choice votes mainly from the incumbent. Counterweight: Alaska polls have overstated Democrats (2020 large miss, 2024 House ~3-4 pts). By Nov 13 most ballots counted; late absentee/rural ballots have historically drifted toward Peltola, so election-night R lead could reverse but not vice versa much.

- Aggregates as of Oct 31: DDHQ Peltola +1.3, FiftyPlusOne +1.9, RCP +1.2 (49.4-48.2).
- Forecasts: DDHQ model Peltola 61%; PoliWave Lean D (+3.5); Cook Toss Up (Oct 30).

- Ballot also includes Heikes (R) — likely draws first-choice votes mostly from R side; Sullivan Jr. (same surname) may draw confused-voter votes from incumbent.
- Historical polling error in Alaska: 2020 Senate polls had Sullivan ~+5, actual ~+12.7; 2024 House polls near-even, Begich led first round ~48.4-45.9; 2022 House polling roughly accurate.
- Count dynamics: election night = polling place + early vote (Oct 19-29); counting continues Nov 4-17; absentees received by Nov 13. In 2022/2024 later-counted ballots tended to shift modestly toward Peltola.
- DOJ suit over certification irrelevant to first-choice displayed totals per fine print.
- Prediction markets exist for final winner (post-RCV) — contract differs from first-choice leader on Nov 13.
- Status quo: no results yet; resolves off Division of Elections ENR page cumulative first-choice totals at 11:59pm AKST Nov 13, not RCV rounds or certified winner.
- Event window: snapshot at Nov 13 23:59 AKST; as of Nov 2 the election has not occurred (0% of counting elapsed).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: recent close Alaska statewide RCV general elections and how far the final polls missed. Final polls give Peltola a lead of about 2-3 points (NYT/Siena 48-46, ASR 48-46 first choice; averages from Peltola +1.2 to +3.0). Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. polls at 3-4% and Heikes takes a little more, mostly at the incumbent's expense on round one. That means Peltola's first-choice lead should be at least as safe as her RCV win; Polymarket's RCV-winner contract has her at about 73-74% ($1.4M volume). It is a near-miss contract (final winner, not the first-choice count on Nov 13), so I treat it as evidence, not an anchor. Late absentee ballots counted Nov 4-13 have historically leaned Democratic (in 2024 Peltola narrowed Begich's election-night lead as counting went on). By Nov 13 nearly all ballots will be counted. The main risk: Alaska polls have often understated Republicans (2020 by a lot, 2024 by about 3-5 points), which would flip a 2-point first-choice lead. The DOJ suit was dismissed Nov 1 and doesn't affect counting anyway.

calls.reasoning: Final first-choice polls show Peltola +2 (NYT/Siena 48-46, ASR 48-46; averages +1.2 to +3.0), and she led the primary 49.5-41.4. The RCV-winner market (~73% Polymarket, ~72% Kalshi) is a near-miss contract that bounds this from below: Heikes and Sullivan Jr. (~6% combined) take round-one votes mainly from the incumbent, so a Peltola first-choice lead is at least as likely as a Peltola win. Ballots counted after election night through Nov 13 have historically leaned Democratic. Main risk: Alaska's historical polling bias toward Democrats (2020, 2024) could flip a 2-point lead.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the late polls, the primary result, the market prices and that they are RCV-winner contracts, the counting schedule, late ballots leaning Democratic, Alaska's pro-Republican polling misses, and the DOJ suit being irrelevant (two runs report it dismissed Nov 1). The only difference is judgment over 1-2 points about how much weight the polling-bias risk gets against the market floor and the first-choice vote-splitting effect. No web access on this run, so nothing new was checked. I agree that P(first-choice lead) >= P(RCV win) ~0.73, plus a small premium for paths where Peltola leads round one but loses after transfers, minus a small amount for D-leaning ballots counted after the Nov 13 cutoff. I land at 0.76. I carry forward Run 3's reference class.
